title: People Ops Playbook: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s people operations standards for hiring, candidate experience, employee onboarding, the performance & feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and front-line managers.

Key goals:
- Maintain a predictable, fair, and efficient hiring process that delivers high-quality candidates.
- Deliver a consistent onboarding experience to accelerate new hire productivity and retention.
- Run a development-focused performance cycle that emphasizes continuous feedback, calibrated reviews, and career development.
- Empower managers with clear responsibilities, checklists, and templates.

1) Hiring process (high level)

Summary: We use a structured, role-based hiring workflow with defined stages, SLAs, and decoupled interview rubrics to reduce bias and ensure repeatability.

Stages and SLA targets (table):
| Stage | Owner | SLA target | Output |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Requisition approved | Hiring manager / People Ops | 3 business days | Live job posting (req ID) |
| Sourcing & screening | Recruiter | 10 business days | 10-20 screened candidates; 3-5 qualified sourcers
| Phone screen (initial) | Recruiter / Hiring manager | 3 business days from screen booking | Screen notes + pass/fail decision |
| Technical interviews | Interview panel | 14 days from screen pass | Interview scorecards + recommendation |
| Manager interview / Final | Hiring manager / peer | 3 business days | Final recommendation |
| Offer & close | People Ops + Hiring manager | 5 business days | Signed offer or rejection note |

Interview matrix and roles:
- Recruiter: manages requisition, candidate communication, scheduling, initial screen.
- Hiring manager: defines rubric, participates in interviews, owns final decision.
- Interviewers (engineers, product, design): use standardized scorecard.
- People Ops: ensures compensation band alignment, background checks, and final offer logistics.

Interview scorecard (required fields):
- Role alignment (yes/no)
- Technical competence (1-5)
- Problem solving (1-5)
- Communication (1-5)
- Collaboration & culture add (1-5)
- Notes & recommendation (hire/hold/no-hire)

Diversity & inclusion practices:
- Use diverse interview panels where possible.
- Require at least one behavioral/structured question per interview.
- Remove demographic identifiers from shared candidate summaries.

2) Candidate experience and offer process

Communication standards:
- Acknowledge application within 48 hours.
- Provide timeline at first contact.
- Send interview prep guide and rubric summary prior to first technical interview.

Offer components and approvals:
- Offer letter template (People Ops) includes: title, base salary, equity summary, bonus (if applicable), start date, manager, primary work location, and key benefits links.
- Compensation approvals: hiring manager -> People Ops compensation partner -> Finance (for out-of-band requests).
- Background check / immigration: initiated after verbal offer acceptance.

3) Onboarding (first 90 days)

Principles: onboarding is a programmatic process owned jointly by Hiring Manager and People Ops to enable fast ramp and psychological safety.

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- People Ops: send welcome packet, IT forms, benefits enrollment links, parking/KMS/office access instructions.
- Manager: share first week plan and 30/60/90 goals, assign a buddy.

Day 1-7 (orientation & setup):
- Day 1: company orientation (People Ops) — company mission, org chart, key systems, security briefing.
- Tech setup: laptop, accounts (Slack, Google, Redwood Console access), VPN, and required compliance trainings.
- Team welcome: intro meeting, 1:1 with manager, buddy pairing.

Week 2-4 (context & contribution):
- Role-specific onboarding checklists (see templates).
- First measurable task assigned with acceptance criteria.
- Weekly 1:1 cadence established.

Month 1-3 (ramp & review):
- 30-day check-in (manager + People Ops): discuss progress, blockers, culture fit.
- 60-day feedback: manager documents progress against 30/60/90 goals.
- 90-day formal onboarding review: decision on continued ramp activities and updated development plan.

Onboarding checklist (sample items):
- Accounts provisioned: [Slack, Google Workspace, Okta, Redwood Console, Jira]
- Security/compliance: [Security training completed, SSO MFA enabled]
- Equipment: [Laptop imaged, monitor, accessories shipped/installed]
- Team integration: [Buddy assigned, onboarding lunches, product demos scheduled]

4) Performance and feedback cycle

Cadence and timeline:
- Continuous feedback: verbal and written notes in weekly 1:1s.
- Quarterly calibration cycles for ICs, semi-annual for managers (timeline published in People Ops calendar).
- Formal performance review: annual deep-review + mid-year calibration (for company-level promotions and compensation).

Review components:
- Self-assessment (required): narrative + examples of impact.
- Manager assessment: competency ratings, impact summary, growth plan.
- Calibration: peer/manager panel to ensure consistency across teams.

Rating scale (example):
- Exceeds expectations (E)
- Meets expectations (M)
- Needs improvement (N)

Promotion & compensation cycle:
- Promotion criteria defined by level ladders and evidence of impact.
- Compensation adjustments tied to market benchmarking and company performance; People Ops publishes budget windows quarterly.

Performance improvement plan (PIP) guidance:
- Use PIPs sparingly and as a clear development tool.
- PIP duration: typically 60-90 days with 2-4 checkpoints.
- Documented expectations, success metrics, and support resources (mentoring, training, role adjustments).

5) Manager responsibilities (checklist)

Hiring:
- Create and maintain accurate job requisitions and role rubric.
- Participate in interview calibration sessions.

Onboarding:
- Provide a 30/60/90 plan on day 1.
- Assign a buddy and schedule regular 1:1s.
- Ensure first measurable contribution is assigned within first 30 days.

Performance & career development:
- Hold weekly 1:1s and document outcomes.
- Give timely feedback (both praise and corrective).
- Run career conversations at least semi-annually.

Compliance & safety:
- Ensure direct reports complete required trainings and security onboarding within 14 days.
- Escalate any harassment or safety issues immediately to People Ops (see Harassment & Safety policy).

6) People policies & standard templates

Included templates (linked internal templates should be copied into the new hire packet):
- Job description template
- Interview scorecard (rubric) template
- Offer letter template (US & EMEA variants)
- 30/60/90 plan template
- Onboarding checklist template
- Performance review template
- PIP template

Policy highlights (summary):
- Time off: PTO accrual, parental leave, and flexible leave policies are in the People Ops Time Off policy page.
- Remote work: hybrid-first with manager-defined core days; people with business-critical needs can request full remote with manager + People Ops approval.
- Travel & expenses: use Concur and follow expense limits in Finance policy.
- Confidentiality & IP: employees sign standard IP assignment and NDA as part of offer acceptance.

Manager quick checklist (first month):
1. Confirm accounts/provisioning.
2. Share team priorities and the 30/60/90 plan.
3. Schedule weekly 1:1s and establish feedback norms.
4. Assign first measurable task and success criteria.
5. Complete 30-day check-in form in People Ops system.

Change history and governance:
- Owners: People Ops (policy steward), Hiring managers (process owners).
- Review cycle: This document is reviewed annually or after material process changes (recruiting tool changes, legal/compliance updates, or leadership changes).
- Contact: people-ops@redwood-inference.internal for questions, template requests, or exceptions.
